what: Simon Property Group owns shopping malls and outlet centres. It is the largest mall landlord in the United States, collecting rent from retailers in its properties and taking stakes in some retail brands.
customers: Retailers and restaurant operators leasing space; shoppers visiting its centres.
money: base rent plus a share of tenant sales at malls and outlets
management fees, and investments in retail brands and international centres
moat: Class A malls in dense, wealthy catchment areas that cannot be rebuilt and that remain the best physical location for many brands.
risks: Department store anchors keep closing and leave large empty space
Debt of about $29 billion is high relative to its equity
Weaker malls in its portfolio face structural decline
opportunities: Occupancy and rents at its best centres have recovered above pre-pandemic levels
Redeveloping anchor space into restaurants, gyms and housing raises income
A dividend yield around 4% is covered by cash flow
watch: Occupancy, the spread between expiring and new rents, and tenant sales per square foot.
